correctness.rationale: The normalized Fourier transform of exp(-lambda r) has the explicit positive constant and decay power; differentiating twice yields Q. The interval minimum is exactly classified by signs of its quadratic coefficient and vertex location, with four exhaustive boundary-consistent branches. The a=0 sharp b-interval follows by an endpoint minimum for b<=0 and an interior vertex for b>0. Continuity plus Bochner shows that any strictly negative spectral region contradicts PSD. Spectral density is positive on an open set at every admissible parameter, yielding strict PD on finite sets. All dimensions and boundary signs are covered analytically; finite arithmetic checks are not used as a proof.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-rate span of Matérn covariance kernels has an exact, complete signed-coefficient admissibility cone rather than merely the sufficient nonnegative-mixture orthant. Its canonical zero-linear-term slice has two distinct sharp spectral-notch endpoints (zero-frequency and spherical) and a genuine Euclidean-dimension phase transition. This explicitly answers which sign-changing or nonconvex mixtures can be valid stationary covariance models, providing a reusable exact design constraint, not an arbitrary single-grid computation. The endpoint and dimension formulas are not simply restatements of generic Bochner positivity.
